name: Active Prime Fix
description: Between a prepared slab and whatever is laid over it sits a primer, and Active Prime Fix is Kerakoll’s rapid universal adhesion promoter for that layer. It is intended under self levelling products, cement based adhesives, finishing products and plasters or renders, so one bucket handles most of the preparation on a fit out instead of three separate primers. What decides whether it suits the job is the substrate: use it where the surface is absorbent and the coat above is cementitious, so suction is evened out and dust is bound in rather than left under the bond. Rapid is the operative word, because the floor can be worked on sooner. Supplied in 5 kg buckets with a 12 month shelf life. In UAE summer conditions a primer film dries quicker than the programme assumes, so confirm it is ready before pouring.

name: Active Prime Grip
description: Active Prime Grip is the quartz finished version of Kerakoll’s rapid universal adhesion promoter, used under self levelling products, cement based adhesives, finishing products and plasters or renders. The quartz finish is the whole reason to choose it over the unfilled grade: on a dense or smooth surface, where there is little suction for a primer to work with, the texture gives the layer above a mechanical key instead of asking adhesion to do everything. So the substrate makes this decision, not the product going over it. It comes in 10 kg buckets and carries a 12 month shelf life. Store it inside rather than in a site container, because a summer in the Emirates will take months off the working life of any water based primer left to cook in the heat.

name: Aqua-Pur Basic
description: Once a hardwood floor is laid and sanded it still has to be protected, and Aqua-Pur Basic is the base coat in that final layer. A base coat is not a thinner version of the finish: it seals the timber, controls how much of the top coat the grain drinks, and settles the colour the finished boards will read as. Kerakoll classes it as a certified, water based varnish, so it is low odour next to a solvent system, which matters when a floor is finished in an occupied apartment or a tower on shared air handling. It carries a 12 month shelf life. Use it beneath an Aqua-Pur top coat rather than alone, and follow the sanding and recoat sequence on the data sheet, because adhesion between coats fails far more often than adhesion to the wood.

name: Aqua-Pur Flex
description: Not every defect in a timber floor can be sanded away. Aqua-Pur Flex is a water based gel for filling defects and deep cracks, used after sanding and before the varnish goes on, so it belongs to the repair step of the finishing sequence rather than to the build up underneath. A gel suits the job better than a paste where the fault is deep or narrow, because it can be worked into the opening and will stay in it. The test is simple: shallow marks disappear under sanding, while anything that would still show through a varnish coat has to be filled first. Supplied in 2 litre cans with a 12 month shelf life. Let the boards acclimatise in the conditioned building before filling, or the gaps filled today will not be the gaps there next month.

name: Aqua-Pur HPX
description: Aqua-Pur HPX is the treatment coat of the Aqua-Pur system, a certified water based varnish for hardwood floors and the layer that actually takes the traffic. Everything below it, the screed, the adhesive and the boards, is protected by this film, so the specification question is how hard the floor will be used and how often it can be taken out of service to be recoated. Being water based it is low odour, which keeps a fit out workable where a solvent finish would mean closing off and venting the area. It has a 12 month shelf life. Apply it over an Aqua-Pur base coat and respect the recoat window on the data sheet. In air conditioned buildings in the Emirates the surface skins quickly, so keep a wet edge and work in manageable bays.

name: Aquaform D
description: Aquaform D is a painted aluminium drip edging, which makes it a profile rather than a waterproofing material in its own right. It is fixed at the open edge of an external balcony or terrace and bonded into the Aquastop Nanoflex, Aquastop Flex or Aquastop Green membrane, so the exposed thickness of the substrate is closed and rainwater is thrown clear of the slab instead of running back underneath the tiling. Edges are where most balcony waterproofing fails, and extra coats of liquid membrane out on the flat will not compensate for an untreated one. Aquaform D is the standard section of three, alongside D Plus and D Small, all covered by one data sheet. On a UAE terrace with railings, set the profile out before tiles are ordered, because changing it later means lifting them.

name: Aquaform R
description: Aquaform R is a site tool rather than a material: a 37 cm wide roller on a stainless steel frame with a handle, carrying a dedicated space for one bag of adhesive as ballast, so the Green-Pro membrane is pressed down evenly and fully across its width. Rolling a sheet membrane by hand gives uneven contact, and the voids left behind the sheet are where water later travels. Weighting the roller to a consistent pressure is what the tool buys. One roller serves many installations, so it is bought once per crew and not by the square metre. It is listed within the waterproofing range because it belongs to that system, but it waterproofs nothing on its own. No data sheet is published for it, so order it by name.

description: Aquaform SD and VD are central drains, used where the floor falls to one point rather than to a line along a wall. name: Aquastop 120
description: Aquastop 120 is a flexible NBR waterproofing joint, not a liquid membrane, and the two are ordered for different reasons. The tape treats perimeter joints and fractionizing joints, the lines where a floor meets a wall or where a large floor is divided, and it is worked into the waterproofing layer so movement along that line does not tear the membrane open. It bonds directly on application. Behind it a liquid product such as Aquastop Nanoflex or Aquastop Flex still has to cover the field of the floor. It is suitable under ceramic and porcelain tiles and natural stone. Order it by linear metre against the measured perimeter, and allow for corners and overlaps, because a run that falls short forces a joint in the wrong place.

name: Aquastop AR1
description: Aquastop AR1 is a reinforcing mesh of alkali resistant glass fibre. Its job is tensile reinforcement inside a coating, not waterproofing: the mesh is embedded in the wet membrane so the cured film carries load across a weak line instead of relying on film thickness alone. Alkali resistance is the whole point of the specification, because ordinary glass fibre degrades in the high pH of cement based products and the reinforcement would then quietly disappear. Use it where a detail needs strengthening rather than everywhere, and keep it distinct from the tapes, which treat movement joints, and from the liquid membranes themselves. It is ordered by roll. Lap the mesh as the data sheet requires and work it fully into the first coat, since mesh left sitting on the surface reinforces nothing.

name: Aquastop BT
description: Aquastop BT is a self adhesive butyl tape, which separates it from an NBR joint bedded into adhesive. The butyl sticks on contact, the face is coated in high adhesion, non woven, alkali resistant polypropylene so a cement based membrane can bond to it, and a pre cut silicone film halfway along the back lets one half be released and fixed while the other stays protected. That is the detail which makes it usable at perimeter joints involving a bituminous sheath, PVC, wood, polycarbonate, glass, plastic or metal, surfaces where a cementitious product has nothing to grip. Choose it for mixed material junctions and keep Aquastop 120 for ordinary perimeter and fractionizing joints. Clean the non porous face thoroughly first, because dust and release oils defeat butyl adhesion.

name: Aquastop Extreme
description: Aquastop Extreme is a reactive waterproofing product, meaning it cures by chemical reaction rather than by drying, and it is specified where the substrate deforms and where chemical attack is expected. High adhesion and high chemical resistance are the two properties Kerakoll puts first, and both point at the same situation: a surface that moves under load or temperature, carrying a finish that cannot be lifted later to make repairs. It is a liquid applied membrane covering the field of a floor or wall, so joints and junctions still need the Aquastop tapes alongside it. Pot life is one hour, so mix in batches matched to the area a crew can cover in that time. Shelf life is 18 months. On a hot UAE site, expect the usable working time to run short of the hour.

name: Aquastop Green
description: Aquastop Green does two jobs at once: it waterproofs, and it decouples. As a decoupling layer it stops cracks in the substrate transferring up into the tile finish, the failure that shows as a straight line of cracked tiles following a crack in the screed below. It also waterproofs over substrates that are already cracked, not fully cured, or still carrying residual moisture and vapour pressure, so a programme need not wait for a screed to dry out completely. It goes down before ceramic tiles, natural stone or hardwood flooring. Applied thickness is 1 to 2 mm, and shelf life is 24 months. Choose it over a plain membrane when substrate movement, rather than water alone, is the risk being managed on that particular floor.

name: Biocalce Fondo
description: Biocalce Fondo is a certified mineral undercoat based on selected pure CL 90-S lime putty to EN 459-1, with selected inert materials, applied before a lime paint or lime finish. Its function is to make the wall uniform. Old plaster absorbs unevenly, and a lime paint taken straight onto it dries at different rates across the surface and reads as patchiness that no second coat fully cures. The undercoat equalises that suction and gives the finish a consistent key. Lime putty keeps the layer vapour permeable and chemically the same as the lime work above and below it, which is the point of staying inside one material family. Supplied in 14 litre buckets with twelve months of shelf life. Stir thoroughly before use, because the inert content settles in the pail.

name: Biocalce Muratura
description: Biocalce Muratura is a breathable mortar based on NHL 3.5 natural hydraulic lime for bedding masonry and dubbing out. On a Gulf structure, where chloride laden moisture drives reinforcement corrosion, preparation matters as much as the mortar: cut back to sound concrete and treat the exposed steel before patching.

name: Joint
description: Joint is neither an adhesive nor a grout but the compressible layer that goes into a movement joint before it is sealed. It is made of closed cell expanded polyethylene, free of CFCs and HCFCs, and is supplied in different degrees of expansion so it serves both as static filling and in joints that have to move. Its other job is to control sealant depth, which is what lets a sealed joint stretch properly instead of splitting. On a UAE terrace or facade the movement joints are where tiling fails first, so size and place these before tiling starts rather than filling the gap afterwards.

name: Remover Pro

name: Silicone
description: Silicone is the transparent sealant in the Kerakoll tiling range, for joints in tile and mosaic work where the sealant should not be seen. Transparent is the honest choice in two situations: against a glass mosaic, where any coloured line reads as a flaw, and on a veined or multicoloured tile that no single sealant colour will match. Perimeters, internal corners, changes of plane and movement joints all need a flexible sealant rather than grout, because that is where the tiling has to move. Cut those joints into the setting out at the start. Grouting them solid and sealing over afterwards is what produces the cracked line along a shower wall.

name: Top Latex
description: Top Latex is an additive, not an adhesive. It is a water based elastic agent mixed into normal and rapid setting mineral adhesives, and the classification quoted against it, C2 E S2, is what the adhesive and the latex achieve together as a system rather than a property of the latex on its own. That upgrade is the reason to use it. S2 deformability means the bed absorbs substrate movement that would crack a rigid one, so a standard adhesive already on site can be brought up to the grade a heated screed or a large format slab demands. Supplied in a 25 kg pack with a 12 month shelf life. Dose it exactly as stated and keep the dose identical in every batch, because a bed mixed at varying latex content will not behave consistently across a floor.

description: Speed without slip is what Adesilex P9 Express is sold on, an improved, fast setting, slip resistant cementitious adhesive of class C2FT to ISO 13007-1. It carries ceramic, porcelain and mosaic indoors and out on floors, walls and ceilings, takes tile over tile up to 900 square centimetres, and holds heavy or large format tiles on a vertical surface without sagging. The programme is the reason to pay for it: 60 minutes of workability, wall joints grouted after 4 hours, floor joints after 6, light foot traffic at about 6 hours and full use after about 3 days. name: Adesilex PG2
description: Adesilex PG2 is a two component thixotropic epoxy adhesive for structural bonding, which places it with the fixing and anchoring products rather than the repair mortars. It bonds and reinforces concrete, natural stone, mortar and brick with very low emissions of volatile organic compounds, certified EMICODE EC1 Plus. Typical work is structural reinforcement of beams and pillars by bonding steel or composite plates to concrete, rigid structural bonding of precast elements, sealing injection ports and surface damage before resin injection, sealing large cracks and repairing joint corners in trafficked industrial floors, bonding fibre reinforced cement slabs and pipes, and bonding TPE strips to concrete for joint waterproofing. Components mix at 3 parts A to 1 part B and consumption is 1.65 to 1.75 kg per square metre per millimetre. Thixotropic means it holds on a vertical face.

name: Antipluviol
description: Antipluviol is an impregnating water repellent rather than a membrane, and that distinction decides where it belongs. Water based and transparent, it soaks into very absorbent masonry and leaves a hydrophobic barrier inside the pores, so driving rain is shed while the wall still breathes and looks unchanged. Exposed brickwork, aerated concrete, renders, skim coats and natural or artificial stone are its substrates, which makes it a facade product and not something for a tank or a buried wall. Consumption follows absorbency, roughly 0.2 to 1 litre per square metre, with render or skim coat nearer 0.20 to 0.80 and tuff stone 0.50 to 1.00. The application window is +5°C to +35°C, so on a UAE site work the shaded elevation and follow the sun round rather than treating a wall that is already baking.

classification: CE EN 1504-2 C PI MC IR
description: Choosing between the Antipluviol grades comes down to how absorbent the surface is, and Antipluviol S is the solvent based one for the tight surfaces. Its extremely high penetration gets it into compact natural stone such as marble, granite, limestone, sandstone and split face stone, and into unglazed ceramic tiles, where a water based repellent would struggle to enter at all. It builds a hydrophobic barrier within the material instead of a surface film, so rain is repelled without altering the appearance or the breathability of the cladding. Being solvent based, ventilate enclosed UAE balconies and shafts while applying, and mask adjacent glazing and polished finishes first.

description: Sitting between the other two grades, Antipluviol W is the water based high penetration repellent for absorbent surfaces. classification: EN 1504-2 coating (C) principles PI, MC and IR
description: Aquaflex Roof HR is a ready to use fibre filled liquid membrane in water emulsion for roofs that stay exposed. White, with a solar reflectance index of 105 to ASTM E1980, 83 per cent solar reflectance and 91 per cent emittance, the sheet states it lowers roof surface temperature by more than half against a dark coloured covering. That is what separates it from the cementitious Mapelastic membranes in our range, which are laid to be tiled or screeded over. Two coats go on, 0.4 to 0.5 mm dry each and never less than 0.8 to 1 mm in total, at a minimum of 2 kg per square metre. Used only as a reflective protective finish over bitumen it drops to 0.5 kg on smooth and 0.9 kg on mineral filled membranes. Two limits decide the job: no membrane newer than six months, and no painted metal.

name: Dynamon MR 2100
description: Dynamon MR2100 is a chloride free hyperplasticising admixture based on polymer modified polycarboxylate ether, added to the mix at the batching plant and not to be confused with anything applied to hardened concrete. It conforms to ASTM C494 as Type G and to EN 934-2, and is aimed at ready mix plants producing high performance concrete by cutting the water to cement ratio. What decides its use is the mix design rather than the structure: it is recommended with GGBS and tri-blend mixes, mass pours that need cohesion, piling mixes, raft foundations and precast work where high early and ultimate strengths are wanted. Normal dosage is 0.8 to 2.5 litres per 100 kg of total cementitious material. Pouring in hot climates is a listed use, which matters on a UAE summer programme.

name: Eco Prim T Plus
description: Priming is the step most often skipped on a floor and most often the reason the levelling layer above it debonds. Eco Prim T Plus is a universal acrylic primer that works on absorbent and non-absorbent substrates alike, which is unusual: it regulates suction on a porous screed so the compound keeps its own mixing water, and it promotes adhesion on dense or already sealed surfaces where a cementitious compound has nothing to grip. It also fixes light dust and isolates gypsum from cement. Supplied as a fluid light blue liquid in 20 kg packs, consumption runs from 30 to 150 g/m² depending on the porosity of the substrate and how it is applied, between +5°C and +35°C. On UAE sites the power floated slab is the usual case, and that is precisely the surface a compound will not bond to unprimed.

name: Elastocolor Paint
classification: CE EN 1504-2 C PI MC IR, EN 15457 GB, EN 15458 GB
description: A render carrying hairline cracks will telegraph them through an ordinary masonry paint within a season. Elastocolor Paint is the elastomeric answer: a one-component acrylic in water dispersion that bridges micro-cracks, stays permeable to vapour while stopping liquid water, and blocks the carbon dioxide that carbonates concrete and corrodes the steel inside it. Testing to EN 15457 and EN 15458 records no growth of mould, fungi or algae, which is the reason it gets specified on shaded and humid elevations. Dilute 10 to 15 per cent with water and lay two coats over the correct primer, 12 to 24 hours apart, at 0.2 to 0.4 kg per square metre per coat. Mapei excludes it from horizontal waterproofing, immersed surfaces and anything walked on. Supplied in 20 kg drums in RAL shades, holding colour change under 2.5 delta E after 1,000 hours of accelerated weathering, which counts on a Gulf facade.

name: Epojet LV
description: Epojet LV is the low viscosity grade of the Mapei two component epoxy injection resin, mixed 3.2 parts A to 0.8 part B into a liquid of 140 mPa.s that runs into microcracks a paste cannot reach, on dry or wet concrete. That is what separates it from Eporip, the fluid paste poured into cracks that have been opened out at 1.35 kg per litre, and from Adesilex PG1 and PG2, which seal the crack face and hold the packers while Epojet LV is pumped in behind them. It meets EN 1504-5 for concrete injection and fills a 0.1 mm crack in 1 minute 30 seconds in dry and in damp sand. Consumption is 1.1 kg per litre of cavity. What decides the job is temperature: never below +10°C, and workability drops from 35 minutes at +23°C to 15 minutes at +30°C.

name: Eporip A+B
description: Eporip is the two component solvent free epoxy Mapei publishes for monolithic construction joints: component A grey and component B white, mixed 3 to 1 into a slightly thixotropic paste and brushed or trowelled onto a dry or slightly damp joint face so the next pour bonds to the old concrete rather than sitting against it. The figure that decides the job is the open time, 3 to 4 hours at +23°C and 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours 30 minutes at +30°C, because the fresh concrete has to be placed inside it and must never be cast onto hardened Eporip. Against Adesilex PG2, the thixotropic grade for bonding plates and precast units, Eporip is the fluid grade for joints and for sealing screed cracks at 1.35 kg per litre of cavity. Cracks narrower than 0.5 mm are widened and dusted out first. Complete hardening takes 7 days.

name: Fugolastic
description: Where a cement joint has to hold its colour and resist absorption, Fugolastic is the liquid polymer gauged into the Keracolor grout range in place of mixing water. It takes the joint to CG2, the improved cementitious class, without moving to a reactive product. The alternative inside the Mapei range is Kerapoxy, and that is the right answer only when the joint faces chemical attack or constant aggressive cleaning. For a bathroom, a villa floor or a mall concourse, a polymer modified cement joint is easier to place, easier to clean off the tile face and far cheaper per square metre. Pot life is around two hours and the joint sets in 24 hours. Supplied as a white liquid in 10 and 25 kg packs, used between 5 and 35 degrees, with 24 months of shelf life.

name: Keralastic
description: Keralastic is a two component polyurethane adhesive from Mapei, classified R2 under EN 12004, for bonding ceramic tiles, stone material and mosaics where cementitious products reach their limits. Being reaction cured, it adheres to screeds, renders and concrete as well as difficult substrates such as wood, metal, PVC, reinforced polyester, fibre cement and gypsum board. It contains no water or solvents, cures without shrinkage and forms a tough, flexible bond that copes with substrate movement. Typical uses include showers, prefabricated bathroom sheets, wooden worktops and mixed substrate refurbishments. For UAE projects involving unusual substrates or wet areas, Keralastic offers a dependable reactive alternative to cement based adhesives. The full technical data sheet with pot life, curing times and consumption can be downloaded from this page.

name: Keralastic T
description: Keralastic T is a two component polyurethane adhesive from Mapei, classified R2 under EN 12004, with a thixotropic consistency that holds tiles on vertical surfaces without slip. It bonds ceramic tiles, stone material and mosaics indoors and outdoors on substrates that defeat cementitious adhesives: wood, metal, PVC, asphalt, reinforced polyester, fibre cement, gypsum and gypsum board as well as ordinary screeds, renders and concrete. Typical UAE uses include showers, prefabricated bathroom sheets, worktops and refurbishments where the existing surface cannot be removed. name: Kerapoxy
description: Kerapoxy is a two component, acid resistant epoxy mortar from Mapei, classified RG under EN 13888 as a grout and R2T as an adhesive. It grouts joints of at least 1 mm in ceramic tile and natural stone floors and walls, indoors and outdoors, and can also be used for acid resistant bonding of tiles, stone, fibre cement and concrete. Cured Kerapoxy resists chemicals, stains and frequent aggressive cleaning, and supports installations that must comply with HACCP food safety requirements. That makes it the reference choice for commercial kitchens, food production areas, laboratories, swimming pools and industrial floors across the UAE. Available in 17 colours. The complete technical data sheet with chemical resistance tables, times and consumption is available for download on this page.

name: Kerapoxy Adhesive
description: Kerapoxy Adhesive is a two component epoxy adhesive from Mapei, classified R2T under EN 12004, an improved reactive adhesive with no vertical slip. The thixotropic consistency holds pieces in position on vertical surfaces while curing. name: Keraset
description: Keraset is a cementitious adhesive for ceramic tiles, produced by Mapei for the UAE market and classified C1 under ISO 13007-1 and EN 12004. It bonds ceramic tiles and mosaics on floors, walls and ceilings in both internal and external applications. The adhesive is easy to trowel, highly thixotropic and hardens without appreciable shrinkage, giving reliable adhesion on traditional render, cement mortar and cured cementitious screeds; anhydrite surfaces can be tiled after priming. Consumption is approximately 2 kg per square metre for mosaics with a number 4 trowel, 2.5 to 3 kg per square metre for normal sizes and around 5 kg per square metre for external floor and wall coverings. name: Lamposilex ME
description: Few products on this line are bought for a single moment, but Lamposilex ME is one of them. It is an ultra fast setting hydraulic binder for stopping water leaks, a grey fine powder gauged in small amounts and pressed into a live leak in concrete or masonry, where it sets while the water is still running. Pot life at +20°C is about one minute, so the operative mixes what fits in a gloved hand and no more. Two figures to work from: 1.8 kg fills a one litre cavity, and it is sold in 5 kg packs that keep for twelve months stored indoors. Its place is post applied below grade waterproofing, where a leak has to be killed before the permanent system goes on. Keep a sealed pack in the site store before basement work starts, not after.

description: Lignobond Chiaro is the light shade of the Mapei two component epoxy polyurethane parquet adhesive, nine parts of component A to one part of component B by weight, with no water and no solvent in it. Hardened at about 24 hours, it bonds to surfaces that are not absorbent, so old ceramic, marble, terrazzo and metal sheet take wood with no separate resin primer, and heated screeds are covered as well. name: Mapeair Foam
description: Dosed through a foam generator rather than straight into the mixer, Mapeair Foam is a ready to use liquid foaming agent for making lightweight foam concrete. Mapei recommends diluting one litre in 50 litres of water; foam produced at 3 bars air pressure has a density of 50 plus or minus 5 kg per cubic metre, so a litre of admixture yields around 1000 litres of foam. The foam is stable enough to be injected into a premixed mortar or grout without collapsing, and the result is self compacting and placed by chute, pipe or pump with no transfer equipment. Below 1000 kg per cubic metre it encases buried services and can be dug out again later; at about 1500 kg per cubic metre it backfills straight from the truck mixer. Protect the drums from direct sunlight.

name: Mapeair LA/P
description: Mapeair LA/P is a powdered foaming agent that entrains a high volume of air into a cement mix, which puts it among the admixtures rather than the repair or sealing products. Added at mixing, it produces lightweight mortar, lightweight concrete and flowable fill: the entrained air cuts density, removes the risk of segregation and gives a mix that stays fluid at a low water content and pumps easily. Typical uses are mortar and concrete made with pumice, expanded clay or polystyrene aggregate for insulation value, super fluid mixes with a low modulus of elasticity, filling ground cuts after pipe laying, and inerting cavities. Average dosage is one 0.5 kg bag per cubic metre of mix. Store in closed containers away from frost and direct sunlight, which on a UAE site means out of the sun.

name: Mapeband
description: A cementitious membrane cannot turn an internal corner on its own, and Mapeband is the tape that lets it. An alkali resistant rubber tape with felt edging, 0.58 mm thick and 120 mm wide, it is bedded fabric side down into a layer of Mapelastic, Mapelastic Smart, Mapelastic Turbo or Mapelastic AquaDefense at least 1 mm thick, with the membrane wetting both flanks. Ultimate elongation of at least 300 per cent and tear resistance of 100 N let a wall to floor junction move rather than split along the line, which is what an untaped junction eventually does. Over a movement joint the tape is set in an omega loop so it can be put in tension. Rolls run 50 m or 10 m, and joints between strips are sealed with Adesilex LP, not with the membrane. Service temperature reaches +60°C, enough for an exposed Dubai terrace.

name: Mapeband Easy H130
description: Mapeband Easy is the 130 mm wide joint tape in the Mapei waterproofing range: a vapour proof, waterproof rubber core sandwiched between two layers of alkali resistant non woven polypropylene, 0.68 mm thick and 285 g/m2, perforated along both edges so the membrane keys through the fabric instead of sitting on it. Against Mapeband, which is 120 mm wide, thinner at 0.58 mm and needs Adesilex LP at the laps, Mapeband Easy is lapped at least 5 cm and bonded with the same waterproofing product as the rest of the detail. It works with the Mapelastic range, Monolastic, Mapegum WPS, the Aquaflex Roof range and Mapeguard UM35. Over a screed control joint that will be tiled, leave the dotted centre strip uncoated and break any reinforcing mesh at the tape edges so the joint can still move. Tensile strength is 45 N per 15 mm at 315 per cent elongation.

name: Mapeband Flex Roll
description: Movement joints and live cracks are where most waterproofing fails, and Mapeband Flex Roll exists to cover them properly. It is a light grey flexible tape, 2.0 mm thick and supplied in 20 metre rolls, bedded into the waterproofing system over expansion joints and cracks so the membrane can carry on across a gap that keeps moving. Elongation at failure is at least 400 per cent both lengthways and across, which is what lets it absorb movement instead of resisting it. Mapei lists it for hydraulic structures, tanks, reservoirs, sewer pipes, bridge decks and post applied below grade waterproofing, so this is detailing material for heavy civil and water retaining work rather than a bathroom tape. Store the rolls dry, dust free and away from aggressive chemicals, which on a UAE site means off the slab and out of the sun.

name: Mapeband Gasket
description: The drain outlet is the commonest point of failure in a wet room, because the membrane has to stop dead at a hole and still be watertight. name: Mapecoat I 600 W
description: Primers decide whether a resin floor lasts, and a water based one widens where it can be used. Mapecoat I 600 W is a two component transparent epoxy primer in water dispersion, mixed 2.3 parts A to 3.6 parts B and applied at 0.15 to 0.50 kg/m² depending on how absorbent and rough the substrate is. It primes industrial resin flooring, sports surface, car park and waterproofing systems, and doubles as an impregnating, salt resistant and dust proof treatment. Vapour permeability is the reason to choose it over a solvent epoxy: it lets a slab release moisture instead of trapping it under the coat. The +8°C to +35°C window suits night work in a UAE summer, when a slab surface sits well above air temperature by mid afternoon.

name: Mapecoat PU 20
description: A waterproofing membrane needs a topcoat above it, and on an exposed deck that topcoat does the ultraviolet work. name: Mapecoat TNS Binder
description: Nothing here goes down neat. Mapecoat TNS Binder is an acrylic resin binder in water dispersion, diluted with 15 to 20 per cent water and then mixed with graded quartz sand to make the paste that actually builds a tennis court, a multi purpose pitch, a cycle track or a footpath. The ratio decides the layer: 40:60 binder to quartz for the one or two filling coats, 50:50 for an intermediate coat, 60:40 for the two or three final coats. Fine sand in the last layer gives a smoother, faster surface and coarse sand a slower one, so pace of play is settled at the mixing bucket. Allow 0.9 to 1.2 kg/m² of concentrated product and 12 to 24 hours between coats. Prime concrete with Mapecoat I 600 W diluted 1:1, and never apply above +35°C.

name: Mapefast HA
description: Mapefast HA is a liquid hardening accelerator for concrete and mortar, classified to EN 934-2 Table 7 and dosed at 0.8 to 4.0 per cent of the weight of the cement. It was developed for mixes carrying fly ash or slag, where early strength is the problem: the hydration heat is released sooner, so the pour reaches the strength it needs before stripping. It is not a plasticiser and the sheet is clear about that, since it leaves the slump, the air content and the workability retention alone, which is why it is combined with a Dynamon superplasticiser rather than used in place of one. It carries no chlorides that could start corrosion in the reinforcement. Add it with the mixing water; straight into a drum mixer it needs one minute of mixing per cubic metre and never less than five.

name: Mapefer
description: Mapefer is not a repair mortar but the step before one: a two component anti-corrosion cementitious coating brushed onto exposed reinforcement once the failed concrete has been broken out. It restores alkalinity around the bar, protects the steel against further corrosion and acts as a bonding promoter for the repair mortar that follows, whether from the Mapegrout range or a cement mortar modified with synthetic resin latex. Skipping it is why repairs fail twice, because the rust that burst the cover off keeps working behind a cosmetically perfect patch. Components mix at 3 parts A to 1 part B into a light blue slurry with about an hour of pot life, applied between 5 and 35 degrees, above or below grade. At a 2 mm coat, allow 120 g per metre on 8 mm bar and 240 g per metre on 16 mm bar.

name: Mapefibre 6 mm
description: Mapefibre 6 mm is loose 6 mm glass fibre dosed into a Mapei self levelling compound on site, one 250 g sachet per bag, stirred in at low speed until the mix is homogeneous and lump free. It is the way to reinforce a plain self leveller from the Ultraplan or Planitex ranges rather than buy a grade that already carries fibre, such as Ultraplan Fiber. The fibres are heat resistant, so they spread evenly through the mix without costing it fluidity, and they are alkali resistant, do not shrink and are not subject to corrosion, which is what lets them stay in a cementitious screed. They distribute through the full thickness of the layer and leave a uniform surface once cured. The sheet keeps them to cementitious or gypsum based self levellers, over anhydrite, concrete, raised floors, OSB and underfloor heating.

name: Mapefibre NS 12
description: Mapefibre NS 12 are 12 mm monofilament polypropylene microfibres, 32 microns across, added at the mixer with the cement, aggregate, water and admixtures to improve the resistance of concrete to cracks caused by plastic shrinkage. The monofilament form is what lets them disperse and distribute through the mix. What decides whether they belong in a specification is printed on the sheet: Mapei states that the fibres offer no structural advantage and may not be considered an alternative to metal reinforcement, so they sit alongside a correct mix design and a proper curing regime rather than in place of either. They also improve fire resistance, durability and the homogeneity of concrete during pouring. The normal dosage is 600 g per cubic metre, which is one bag, and higher dosages are used for shotcrete and fire resistance.

name: Mapefill GP ME
description: Mapefill GP ME is a general purpose, non shrink cementitious grout classified to EN 1504-6, used to fill the gap between something fixed and the structure holding it. Non shrink is the whole point: an ordinary cement mix contracts as it cures and leaves the base plate it was meant to support bearing on nothing. It grouts honeycombing in concrete, fills gaps in precast elements, beds base plates and bridge bearings, anchors machinery, steel bolts and metallic fixtures, fills rigid joints and serves underpinning and pressure grouting. For precast elements and rigid joints the thickness should not exceed 60 mm. A flowable mix takes 3.8 to 3.9 kg of water per bag, giving a flow of under 60 seconds to ASTM C939, and each 25 kg bag yields 13 to 14 litres. Pour from one side only so air is driven ahead of the grout.

name: Mapeflex AC4
description: Mapeflex AC4 is a paintable acrylic sealant for internal and external expansion and construction joints with a medium amount of movement, and for surface cracks in absorbent building materials. description: Mapeflex PSU SL ME is the self levelling grade of a multi component polysulphide joint sealant, poured into horizontal joints in floors and other level surfaces where the level tolerance is within 3 per cent, rather than gunned onto a vertical face. Polysulphide gives a tough rubber like seal that accommodates continuous and pronounced cyclic movement of plus or minus 25 per cent, which is why the range is specified for movement joints in buildings, industrial floors, car parks, subways and infrastructure work. Joints from 5 to 50 mm wide can be sealed, and trafficked joints or those under hydrostatic pressure should be designed to around 20 mm. Shore A hardness runs from 17 to 22 and pot life is 120 minutes at 25 degrees. For a water retaining structure the non sag grade is specified instead of this one.

name: Mapeflex PU 45 FT
description: Heavy traffic is where Mapeflex PU 45 FT earns its place: a paintable, rapid, high modulus polyurethane sealant and adhesive for expansion and distribution joints in horizontal and vertical surfaces, including joints occasionally attacked by hydrocarbons. Movement capability is 20 per cent of joint width, classified F20 HM to ISO 11600, and the application list is explicit about traffic, covering industrial floors taking heavy vehicles, car parks, supermarkets, shopping centres and warehouses, and ceramic floors where fork lifts run. Its thixotropic consistency lets it hold in a vertical joint as well. Used as an adhesive up to 3 mm it bonds cement based materials, brick, metals, glass, gypsum, wood, ceramics and plastics. Shore A hardness is 40 and cartridges are 600 ml. Rapid hardening shortens the time a joint has to stay closed to site traffic.

name: Mapeflex PU 65
description: Mapeflex PU 65 is a two component castable polyurethane elastomeric sealant for road joints finished flush with the surface, developed for highway construction joints and for filling and sealing the anchoring heads of pre-formed rubber, reinforced rubber and steel road joints between adjacent decks and between deck and abutment. It is a trafficked product in the fullest sense, suitable for vehicles on roads, freeways and highways, and it also serves as a connection sealant between a prefabricated road joint and the adjoining bituminous conglomerate. Shore A hardness of 80 is the figure that sets it apart: this is for substrates subject to limited movement and heavy load rather than a flexing building joint. Set to foot traffic takes about 2 to 3 hours, the application range is 0 to 35 degrees, and mineral fillers may be added after mixing.

name: Mapeflex PU 70 SL
description: Fuel is the deciding factor with Mapeflex PU 70 SL, a two component free flowing elastic polyurethane sealant poured into expansion and contraction joints in concrete floors that come into accidental or intermittent contact with petrol, diesel, aviation spirit, lubricants and de-icing substances. It is a horizontal product, poured into joints with a slope of up to 2.5 per cent, and the joint has to be designed so that movement in service stays within 25 per cent of its initial width. Runways, car parks, service areas, mechanical workshops, roads, courtyards, ports and logistics areas with moving vehicles are its ground, along with run off tanks in refineries, fuel depots and petrochemical plants. Components mix at 66 to 34 by weight, Shore A hardness is 18, and Mapefoam backer cord sets the depth of the sealant.

name: Mapeflex PU S25
description: Mapeflex PU S25 is a low modulus elastic polyurethane sealant developed for internal and external vertical expansion and construction joints, classified F-25 LM to ISO 11600. Low modulus is the selection point: it carries movement up to 25 per cent of joint width while putting very little stress back into the joint edge, with a modulus of elasticity of 0.20 N per square millimetre, which suits weaker or brittle substrates that a high modulus sealant would tear away. Its thixotropic consistency makes it quick to gun on a vertical face, and it can be painted over once hardened, subject to preliminary tests. Shore A hardness is 20, the working range 5 to 40 degrees, and cartridges hold 600 ml in beige, grey and white. For a trafficked floor joint choose a high modulus polyurethane instead of this one.

name: Mapefloor Binder 930
description: Resin bound paving is a mortar mixed on site from aggregate and binder, and the binder decides how it behaves. Mapefloor Binder 930 is a one component aliphatic polyurethane binder for decorative floors, colourless and transparent so the natural aggregate shows rather than a pigment. Consumption is roughly 0.8 to 1.0 kg/m² per centimetre of mortar thickness, depending on the type and absorbency of the aggregate, and it is batched by weight against 2 to 4 mm stone. Aliphatic chemistry keeps it from yellowing outdoors. Careful traffic is possible after eight hours. Supplied in 5 kg packs with a 12 month shelf life above +5°C. In the UAE it suits permeable landscape paving, where surface water drains through the mortar instead of running to a gully.

name: Mapefloor Cleaner ED
description: This one is not a layer of the floor at all, it is how the floor is kept. Mapefloor Cleaner ED is a concentrated water soluble degreasing detergent built on low foaming surfactants, with terpinolene adding a solvent and deodorising action, supplied as a green liquid in 10 kg cans. It is diluted at 1 to 3 per cent, meaning 100 to 300 g in ten litres of water, and the concentration goes up on porous or heavily soiled surfaces. Mapei wrote it for resin floors such as the Mapefloor System and for the protective films on Ultratop decorative floors, by hand or by machine, and limits it to surfaces water cannot damage. The concentrate sits at pH 11.3 with 12 per cent active substances. Store between +10°C and +30°C, which in the UAE means a conditioned store rather than a site container.

name: Mapefloor Finish 415 ME
description: Finishes in a resin build up split into two families, and this one belongs indoors or beneath another coat. Mapefloor Finish 415 ME is a two component aromatic polyurethane finish, coloured, flexible and wear resistant, mixed 80 parts A to 20 parts B and applied at a theoretical 0.3 to 0.8 kg/m². Aromatic chemistry is tough but not ultraviolet stable, so it belongs on intermediate car park decks and enclosed industrial floors rather than on an exposed top deck where an aliphatic grade is required. Flexibility is why polyurethane is used here instead of epoxy: it moves with a deck instead of cracking along it. Gel time is 60 minutes at +23°C and set time 24 hours. description: A poured repair rather than a hand applied one, Mapegrout ME05 is a high flow, shrinkage compensated micro concrete classified R4, placed in sections from 15 mm up to 220 mm. Typical work is pile top treatment and re profiling, column jacketing, structural reinstatement of beams and columns, honeycombed concrete, floor beams and slabs, and grouting of precast elements, machine and turbine baseplates, bridge bearings and crane rails. It mixes at 2 parts A to 1 part B and goes on by trowel or roller at about 1.6 kg per square metre per millimetre, or by rendering machine at about 2.2, from a 30 kg kit. An exposed UAE terrace swings a long way between night and afternoon, which makes the flexible grade the sensible specification over a rigid one.

description: Mapelastic Zero is the CO2e fully offset edition of the Mapei two component cementitious waterproofing mortar, a 24 kg bag of grey powder to an 8 kg jerrycan of liquid mixed 3 to 1. name: Mapelux Lucida
description: The last layer of a floor build up is the one that gets renewed. Mapelux Lucida is a cross linked high strength metallic wax with a shiny finish, applied at 50 g/m² as part of routine cleaning and maintenance rather than as part of the floor itself. A sacrificial wax takes the scuffing and the cleaning chemicals so the resin or cementitious surface beneath it does not, and it is stripped and reapplied on a cycle instead of being repaired. Cross linking is what gives it enough strength to be worth applying on a commercial floor at all. It is applied between +10°C and +30°C and supplied in 10 kg units with a 12 month shelf life. For a UAE retail unit, set the renewal cycle against footfall, not the calendar.

name: Mapelux Opaca
description: Gloss is a maintenance decision as much as a design one, and this is the matt option. Mapelux Opaca is a cross linked high strength metallic wax with a matt finish, applied at 50 g/m² as part of a routine cleaning and protection regime. It does the same sacrificial job as the shiny grade: it absorbs the scuffs and the cleaning chemicals, then gets stripped and reapplied rather than mended. A matt film also hides scratching and uneven light far better than gloss, which is why it suits a large open floor under strong lighting. Application runs from +10°C to +30°C, in 10 kg units with a 12 month shelf life. In the UAE, matt also means less glare from sunlight coming through a shopfront.

name: Mapenet 150
description: Reinforcement is what keeps a coating whole over a substrate that moves, and Mapenet 150 is the mesh that provides it. Alkali resistant glass fibre to the ETAG 004 guide, blue, 150 g/m² with a 4 by 4.5 mm aperture, it is laid into the fresh first layer of Mapelastic, Mapelastic Smart, Mapelastic Turbo or Monolastic and pressed in with a trowel until fully embedded, with each piece overlapped by at least 5 cm. Breaking strength is above 32 N/mm in warp and weft, and still at least 20 N/mm after ageing in alkaline solution, which matters because it spends its life inside cement. Besides holding cracks closed it helps the applicator keep the layer even. Rolls are 50 m by 1 m. On an exposed UAE terrace it also improves the system against the daily temperature swing and abrasion.

name: Mapeproof AL
description: Mapeproof AL is a sheet membrane rather than a coating: a self adhesive HDPE waterproofing membrane that bonds fully to concrete cast against it, used to waterproof underground structures after the pour. name: Mapeproof Liquid Membrane
description: Sheet membranes are strong on long flat runs and weak at penetrations, and Mapeproof Liquid Membrane is the two component polyurethane elastomer that finishes those details. It is thixotropic, so it stays where it is put on a vertical face, and it seals, fills and details Mapeproof AL and Mapethene HT and LT membranes at pipes, corners and terminations. Elongation at failure is 440 per cent to ISO 37 and bond strength to concrete is 2 N per square millimetre to EN 1542, which is why it can be trusted at the junction between two systems. Mix at 100 parts A to 25 parts B, allow about 1.2 kg per square metre per millimetre on smooth concrete and build at least 2.5 mm on system details. Finish every detail before protection boards go up: none of it is reachable once concrete arrives.

description: Mapeproof Primer does a job that sits slightly apart from the rest of this line. name: Mapeproof Swell
description: Pipes and conduits passing through a waterproofed wall are a known leak path, and Mapeproof Swell is the hydrophilic sealant made for them. Supplied as a light grey thixotropic paste in 320 ml tubes and extruded with a standard gun, it is hydro expansive: it takes up water and swells against the gap it occupies, so the seal tightens under the very conditions that defeat a passive one. Elongation above 700 per cent to DIN 53504 lets it move with the structure, and one tube runs to roughly three linear metres of bead. Mapei lists it for swimming pools, hydraulic structures, tanks, reservoirs, sewer pipes and post applied below grade waterproofing. Confine the bead as the sheet shows, and store the tubes between +15°C and +25°C, which on a UAE site means the office rather than the container.

name: Mapequick AF 70
description: An accelerator rather than a repair product, Mapequick AF 70 is a liquid alkali free admixture dosed into sprayed concrete so that shotcrete sets quickly and gains strength after a very short curing time. It works in both wet mix and dry mix spray systems and conforms to ASTM C1141 and EN 934-5. The absence of alkali is the reason to choose it: concrete develops high mechanical resistance within minutes of placing with almost no loss of final strength against an unaccelerated mix, and the handling risk of an alkaline accelerator goes away. Dosage by weight is 3 to 10 kg per 100 kg of cement. Typical work is securing surfaces during tunnelling, consolidating rock and cliff faces, structural tunnel repairs and final linings. description: Mapeset is a fast setting, cementitious tile adhesive from Mapei, classified C1 under EN 12004 and ISO 13007-1. name: Mapesil LM
description: Stone is the reason Mapesil LM exists: a neutral, solvent free silicone with a low modulus of elasticity, formulated so that no surface bleeding or plasticiser migration can stain marble, granite, sandstone or quartz. name: Mapesilent
description: Acoustic failure between apartments is usually structural contact rather than a thin floor. Mapesilent Panel is a dry soundproofing tile one metre square and 13 mm thick, a bitumen and polymer elastoplastomeric membrane sandwiched with polyester fibre, laid fibre side down on the slab and screeded over. name: Mapestone PFS 2 Visco
description: Mapestone PFS 2 Visco is the pourable jointing grout of the Mapei Mapestone system for stone and concrete paving driven on by vehicles, and not a tile grout. It is a ready mixed powder in 25 kg bags, gauged with only 3 to 3.5 litres of water into a fluid slurry and spread over damp stone with a rubber rake. The low viscosity is the point: it runs to the bottom of the joint and into the contact faces of the block, taking out the air pockets left when the stone was bedded, so the joint anchors the block instead of just closing it. name: Mapetard RCC ME
description: Mapetard RCC ME is a liquid retarding admixture with a plasticising effect, used to hold a cementitious mix workable rather than to speed anything up. Added at batching, it inhibits setting so that workability is maintained for up to 72 hours after the mix is batched, which is why it belongs with long transport runs, pumping from the surface, delays in injecting and any grout that cannot be placed in one shift. It conforms to ASTM C494. Supplied in bulk, in 1000 litre IBCs and in 25 kg jerrycans, with a two year shelf life in closed containers kept above 5 degrees and out of direct sunlight. Heat shortens the working life of every cementitious mix, so on a UAE site this admixture is doing in reverse exactly what the weather does, and it earns its place in summer grouting.

name: Mapewrap 21
description: MapeWrap 21 is a two component, super fluid epoxy resin used to impregnate MapeWrap fabrics immediately before they are placed on concrete, reinforced concrete or masonry for repair or strengthening. It belongs to the composite strengthening system rather than to the mortar or sealant ranges: the fabric carries the load, and the resin saturates it and bonds it to the prepared substrate. Super fluid consistency is what makes it the damp system resin, with the fabric wetted out as it goes on. Adhesion to concrete exceeds 3 N per square millimetre after 7 days at 23 degrees, with failure occurring in the concrete rather than at the bond line. The working range is 10 to 30 degrees, which on a UAE facade usually means early morning work. Supplied in 5 kg units with a 24 month shelf life.

name: Mapewrap 31
description: Used for the dry system, MapeWrap 31 is a two component epoxy adhesive of medium viscosity applied to the prepared surface so that the MapeWrap fabric is laid into it and rolled through, rather than being saturated beforehand. It serves the same purpose as the rest of the system, repairing or strengthening concrete, reinforced concrete and masonry elements with composite fabric, but the paste consistency of component A holds on a vertical face where a super fluid resin would run. Adhesion to concrete is greater than 3 N per square millimetre after 7 days, with failure in the concrete. The working range is 5 to 30 degrees and shelf life is 24 months at not below 5 degrees. Consumption depends entirely on which fabric is specified, so take it from the system schedule rather than estimating it.

name: Mapewrap C Fiocco
description: Structural connections are the whole job of MapeWrap C FIOCCO, a unidirectional high strength carbon fibre cord inside a protective gauze sheath, supplied in 6, 8, 10 and 12 mm diameters on 10 m rolls. One end is impregnated with MapeWrap 21 super fluid epoxy, broadcast with dry quartz sand and pushed into a drilled hole already filled with MapeWrap epoxy grout or a Mapefix chemical anchor; the free end is splayed out and bonded over the element being tied, in concrete, stone, brick or tuff. It anchors Mapegrid mesh and MapeWrap or Carboplate strengthening so the reinforcement cannot peel away. Fibre tensile strength is 4,830 N per square millimetre, but hole size, cord diameter and spacing come from the strengthening design and only the project engineer sets them. Over coat the finished system, since the listed coatings screen UV in direct sunlight.

name: Mapewrap Primer 1
description: Every MapeWrap application starts here. MapeWrap Primer 1 is a two component epoxy primer formulated for the system and used to prepare concrete, reinforced concrete or masonry before the fabrics are bonded, a step the system treats as necessary rather than optional. It consolidates the surface and gives the impregnating resin a sound base, which is why pull off results on the finished build up exceed 3 N per square millimetre after 7 days at 23 degrees with failure in the concrete. Consumption is 250 to 300 g per square metre, supplied in 2 kg units with a 24 month shelf life. The working range is 10 to 30 degrees. name: Monofinish
description: Smoothing rather than structural repair is what Monofinish is for: a one component, normal setting cementitious mortar trowelled onto concrete and cement render at a maximum of 2 to 3 mm per coat. It evens out surface imperfections before painting, levels off concrete that has been repaired with mortars from the Mapegrout range, and smooths irregular render that is otherwise mechanically sound. The thickness limit is the selection rule. If the defect is deeper than a few millimetres the surface needs a reprofiling mortar first, because a fairing coat applied too thick will craze and debond. Consumption is 1.4 kg per square metre per millimetre of thickness, supplied in 22 kg bags with a twelve month shelf life in dry storage. On a UAE facade, work out of direct sun so the mortar does not flash off before it is closed.

name: Nivoplan
description: Nivoplan is the cement, selected aggregate and synthetic resin powder Mapei uses to render and level walls and ceilings in layers from 2 to 20 mm, classified GP category CS IV to EN 998-1. The thickness band is the reason to choose it over Monofinish in our range, which is a fairing coat limited to 2 to 3 mm a pass. Two rules on the sheet decide the job. name: Nivorapid

name: Planicrete
description: Planicrete is a synthetic rubber latex gauged into cement mixes to improve their adhesion and mechanical performance, so it modifies a mortar rather than being one. It is used as an admixture in cement based screeds, renders and thin smoothing layers, and in highly adhesive cement bonding slurries. Typical work includes high strength screeds and renders inside and out, bonding slurries that let a new screed hold onto an existing one, cementitious slurry for laying natural stone with the Mapestone system, adhesive shotcrete for bonding renders, and mortars for filling holes and finishing precast elements. It is applied between 5 and 40 degrees, supplied in 25 kg and 5 kg containers, and keeps for 24 months unopened. Where the finished surface takes abrasion, such as a ramp or a channel, the latex earns its cost several times over.

name: Planicrete SP
description: Planicrete SP is a multipurpose latex additive for mortars and a component of cementitious mortar adhesives, which places it with the mix modifiers and not with the repair or sealing ranges. Gauged into a mix it produces high performance mortar, screeds and renders: high resistance screeds and levelling compounds for interior and exterior use, cement renders, high adhesion cement slurry for bonding new screeds onto existing screeds and concrete, and cement mortar adhesive for fixing ceramic tiles on walls and floors. Against a cementitious precision grout such as Mapefill GP ME it buys strength and chemistry, 90 MPa in compression and 28 MPa in flexure at seven days, with a bond to concrete above 3 MPa that fails in the concrete, not at the joint, which is why the sheet puts it under pumps, presses, crane rails and tie rod anchors that carry vibration. name: Planiseal 88
description: An osmotic mortar works differently from a flexible coating. Planiseal 88 is a cementitious powder that seals masonry and concrete by forming crystals within the pores of the substrate itself, which is why it is suitable for contact with drinking water and classified to EN 1504-2 as MC IR. It suits stable structures such as potable water tanks and below grade walls rather than a roof or balcony that moves, because an osmotic mortar is rigid by nature. Mix 100 parts powder with 21 to 23 parts water, 5.25 to 5.75 litres per bag, allow about an hour of pot life and 1.5 kg per square metre per millimetre of thickness, from 25 kg bags. The application range reaches +40°C, generous for the Gulf, but shelf life shortens in heat and humidity, so rotate stock.

name: Planiseal WR 100
classification: CE EN 1504-2 C PI MC IR
description: Planiseal WR 100 protects reinforced concrete without covering it. A ready mixed, pure silane based hydrophobising liquid, it migrates into the surface and leaves a water repellent zone inside the concrete, so chloride bearing water is kept out while the surface keeps its appearance. That makes it a durability treatment for structures exposed to aggressive agents, chlorides in particular, which is the mechanism behind most reinforcement corrosion in coastal Gulf concrete. It goes onto vertical and horizontal surfaces, onto porous or compact concrete, onto new work and onto concrete already repaired, at roughly 0.1 to 0.2 kg per square metre per coat from 5 kg units. It is CE marked to EN 1504-2. Treat the surface once repairs have cured and the concrete is dry, because a silane needs open pores to migrate into.

name: Primer G
description: Primer G is a synthetic resin primer in water dispersion, and what it does explains why no levelling layer should be poured without one. It evens out the absorption of the substrate so the compound above does not lose its mixing water into the slab and cure weak and dusty, it binds residual dust, and on gypsum or anhydrite it forms a film that prevents the sulphate reaction with cement which otherwise separates the two layers. Use it before smoothing compounds on cementitious, anhydrite and gypsum surfaces, and between coats of smoothing compound once the first is dry. Supplied as a light blue liquid in 25 kg and 5 kg packs, consumption is 0.08 to 0.15 kg/m² depending on porosity, applied from +5°C to +35°C. name: Primer LT
description: Primer LT is a light blue acrylic water based primer at 43% dry solids, written by Mapei for one family of jobs: priming absorbent indoor surfaces before Ultratop Loft and Mapei cementitious skimming mortars, and priming between the layers of Ultratop Loft itself. Against Primer G it is the narrower choice, internal surfaces only, ruled out on magnesium substrates and wherever capillary rising damp is present, and allowed on wood only where the boards are stable and will never meet water. The substrate sets the dilution by weight: 1:1 between Ultratop Loft layers, 1:2 on cementitious or anhydrite, neat on wood. Consumption is about 0.1 kg/m2 between Loft layers and 0.1 to 0.2 kg/m2 on other substrates. It dries in 15 to 20 minutes and is overcoated at 2 to 3 hours, never later than 24.

name: Primer MF (a+b)
description: Primer MF is the two component solvent free epoxy primer Mapei publishes as a residual moisture barrier, predosed three parts A to one part B and applied at 0.2 to 0.4 kg/m2 per coat. Primer MF goes over concrete slabs and cementitious screeds reading up to 6% CM or 100% RH, and up to 3% CM or 50% RH on heated screeds, before moisture sensitive wooden and resilient floors are laid. The hygrometer reading and the finish decide it. A barrier needs a continuous film, so at least two coats about three hours apart, the first by trowel and the second by roller; one coat is enough where the job is only to consolidate a weak or dusty screed. name: Primer SN A+B
description: Primer SN is the two component fillerized epoxy primer under the Mapefloor resin systems, the Ultratop and Ultratop Loft ranges and resin mortar screeds. name: Prosfas
description: Prosfas is a water based blend of silicates, not an acrylic primer, and that difference decides when it is the right call. Its low viscosity carries it several centimetres into a cementitious substrate, where it dries and improves the cohesion of the surface, so it is the product for a screed that dusts or crumbles because it was short of binder or because hydration went wrong. Eco Prim T Plus regulates suction and promotes adhesion, but it leaves a weak screed weak. Prosfas is ready to use and must never be diluted, and it is ruled out on non absorbent or wet surfaces, on anhydrite, and on Mapecem and Mapecem Pronto screeds. Allow 0.5 to 0.7 kg per square metre on a screed surface, four to six times that on a very porous one, applied between +5°C and +35°C.

name: Pulicol 2000
description: Pulicol 2000 is a gel of unchlorinated solvents for stripping old natural and synthetic resin adhesives, paint and grout residue off marble, ceramic, wood, concrete, cementitious levelling coats, gypsum and metal. Because it is a gel it stays where it is spread with a trowel or brush, and the sheet notes it gives off very little odour. Waiting time is what the job turns on: about 5 to 10 minutes on acrylic or vinyl adhesives in water dispersion, about 45 to 60 minutes on reactive, polyurethane or epoxy polyurethane adhesives, then scrape it back and either rinse with plenty of water or sand it. Where UltraCare Epoxy Off Gel lifts cured epoxy grout off a tile face, this strips the adhesive film off the substrate underneath. It is flammable, so rubber, PVC, solvent sensitive enamel and varnished wood floors are ruled out. Coverage is 0.3 kg per square metre.

name: Quartz
description: Quartz is Mapei's selected silica sand, graded by particle size and sold for mixing into epoxy and polyurethane resin rather than into cement. name: Ultracare Acid Cleaner
description: UltraCare Acid Cleaner is the concentrated acid detergent in the range, bought to deal with cementitious residue a neutral product will not shift: hardened grout, salt and lime scale efflorescence, rust marks and organic dirt left after installation. It is cleared for ceramics, porcelain, glass mosaic and acid resistant natural stone, and that last qualifier decides everything. On polished marble, or any acid sensitive stone, the correct product is the neutral UltraCare Multicleaner instead, because an acid will dull the surface permanently. Dilution governs strength and therefore coverage, so a test area comes before the first wall. Hard water leaves heavy lime scale in UAE wet areas, which is exactly what this is good at. A transparent liquid in 1 and 5 litre packs, used from zero to 40 degrees, with four years of shelf life.

name: Ultracare Keranet
description: UltraCare Keranet is the buffered acid concentrate Mapei publishes for washing cement off a finished floor: grout residue, installation dirt, limescale, rust marks and salt efflorescence. It is diluted 1 part to 5 or 10 parts water by weight, left to act about five minutes, worked with a single disc machine or an emulsifying pad and rinsed with clean water, and it goes on undiluted to strip engobbio from porcelain. The acid is as aggressive on efflorescence as muriatic or sulphuric acid without their toxic fumes, and used properly it does not damage a coloured cement joint. The tile decides it. Acid resistant materials only: porcelain, ceramic, glass mosaic, quarry tile, terracotta and acid resistant stone. Polished marble, limestone, cementitious terrazzo and non acid resistant glazes are ruled out. Grout must be cured, one to ten days; for residue at the point of laying Mapei specifies UltraCare Keranet Easy.

name: Ultracare Rust Remover
description: Rust is the only stain this bottle is for. UltraCare Rust Remover is a fast acting, acid free cleaner in aqueous solution with a slightly alkaline pH of 7.5, and that is precisely why it can be used on acid sensitive materials such as limestone, polished limestone included, where an acidic descaler would etch the surface beyond saving. description: Before a protective finish goes over an Ultratop, Ultratop Living or Ultratop Loft surface, Ultratop Base Coat prepares it, and that preparation decides how the finish will look. A decorative cementitious surface is unevenly porous, so a finish laid straight onto it is absorbed at different rates and dries patchy. This one component acrylic primer in water dispersion seals those pores and regulates absorption so the finish lies down evenly, and being transparent it does not alter the appearance of the coating beneath. description: An epoxy joint earns its price in four places, and the Morcemcolor Epoxi sheet names them: water submerged areas, surfaces holding aggressive chemicals, food, pharmaceutical and hygiene rooms, and floors under heavy traffic. The numbers behind the premium are compressive strength of at least 45 N/mm2, flexural of at least 30, abrasion under 250 mm3 and water absorption of 0.1 g or less at four hours, far tighter than the cementitious grades. Two cautions matter in the UAE: pot life is 60 minutes at 25 degrees and shortens as temperature climbs, and an external substrate must be below 40 degrees before grouting starts. 5 kg packs.

name: Paviland Primer Ceramic
description: A primer is chosen by what lies underneath, not by preference, and Paviland Primer Ceramic is the one for a floor that will not absorb anything: an existing ceramic or stoneware tile floor, stoneware, marble, stone, terrazzo, polished cement or very low porosity concrete. It is ready to use and must not be diluted, because the hard red film it leaves carries fine quartz aggregate that gives a cementitious levelling compound something mechanical to grip. Roll it thin and even with a medium pile roller and leave no puddles. Drying is about 90 minutes on a non-absorbent subfloor and 12 hours on calcium sulphate floors, gypsum fibre boards and sanded mastic asphalt screed. Coverage is 125 g/m2 from a 10 kg jerry can, applied between 15 and 35 degrees Celsius. Lay the levelling compound within 24 hours, while the film is still clean.

name: Paviland Primer Epoxy
description: Reach for a resin primer when there is a reason, and here the reason is moisture. Paviland Primer Epoxy is a solvent free and water free two component epoxy that penetrates deeply, strengthens a weak substrate and reduces the vapour diffusion rate on cement and concrete floors holding residual moisture of up to 5 CM per cent, which a dispersion primer cannot do. Part B is poured into Part A, 2.85 kg into 7.15 kg, and the mix has 45 minutes at 25 degrees Celsius or 30 minutes at 30. name: Paviland Primer R
description: Dilution is how this primer adapts to the floor it is given. Paviland Primer R is a dispersion primer for the absorbent cementitious substrate, which is the ordinary case under a Paviland self levelling compound, and it both seals and binds: it penetrates, hardens a dusty screed and leaves an evenly absorbent surface, so the compound above keeps its own mixing water and does not blow pinholes or bubbles. On a moderately absorbent or non-porous floor, dilute 1:1 with clean water. On a medium to highly porous one, prime twice, 1:3 first and 1:1 second, at roughly 100 and 200 g/m2 in turn, from a 10 kg jerry can. Brush, roller and airless spray all work. It dries in one to two hours on an absorbent substrate, longer on a dense one, and is rated over underfloor heating.
